questions.q: Who made Uzziah king after the death of his father Amaziah?
questions.a: The people of Judah took Uzziah and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.

questions.q: What did Uzziah do to the town of Eloth after he became king?
questions.a: Uzziah rebuilt Eloth and restored it to Judah.

questions.q: How did Uzziah follow the example of his father in his relationship to Yahweh?
questions.a: Uzziah did what was right in the eyes of Yahweh and set himself to seek God.

questions.q: What happened to Uzziah as long as he sought Yahweh?
questions.a: As long as Uzziah sought Yahweh, God made him prosper.

questions.q: What was the result of God helping Uzziah as he fought against his enemies?
questions.a: God helped Uzziah fight against his enemies, and his fame spread to other lands, and he became very powerful.

questions.q: What did Uzziah build at the gates in Jerusalem and in the wilderness?
questions.a: Uzziah built towers at the corner gates of Jerusalem and at the turning wall. He also built watch towers in the wilderness.

questions.q: Why did Uzziah build watch towers, and why did he dig cisterns in the wilderness?
questions.a: Uzziah built watch towers and dug cisterns in the wilderness because he had cattle and people who farmed and he loved farming.

questions.q: How did Uzziah’s army make war?
questions.a: Uzziah’s army made war with mighty power to help the king against the enemy.

questions.q: How did Uzziah’s army make war?
questions.a: Uzziah’s army made war with mighty power to help the king against the enemy.

questions.q: What was invented by skillful men in Jerusalem as Uzziah equipped his army?
questions.a: In Jerusalem, Uzziah built engines that were invented by skillful men.

questions.q: How far did Uzziah’s fame spread when he was greatly helped by Yahweh, until he became very powerful?
questions.a: Uzziah’s fame spread to distant lands.

questions.q: How did Uzziah trespass against Yahweh, his God, when he became powerful?
questions.a: Uzziah trespassed against Yahweh when he went into the house of Yahweh to burn incense on the altar of incense.

questions.q: Why did Azariah and the eighty priests go in after Uzziah, and why did Azariah say that Uzziah had trespassed when he burned incense in the sanctuary?
questions.a: The priests told Uzziah that it is only the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to burn incense in the sanctuary, so Uzziah had trespassed when he burned incense to Yahweh.

questions.q: What happened to Uzziah as he was holding a censer in his hand to burn incense, and when he was angry with the priests?
questions.a: While Uzziah was holding a censer, and when he became angry with the priests, leprosy broke out on his forehead.

questions.q: Why did leprosy break out on Uzziah’s forehead?
questions.a: Leprosy broke out on Uzziah’s forehead because Yahweh had struck him.

questions.q: Why did Uzziah have to live in a separate house until the day of his death?
questions.a: Uzziah had to live in a separate house because he was a leper and he was cut off from the house of Yahweh.

questions.q: Who became king after Uzziah died and was buried with his ancestors?
questions.a: Jotham, Uzziah’s son, became king in his place.

commentary.text: Verses 1–15 As long as Uzziah sought the Lord, and minded religion, God made him to prosper. Those only prosper whom God makes to prosper; for prosperity is his gift. Many have owned, that as long as they sought the Lord, and kept close to their duty, they prospered; but when they forsook God, every thing went cross. God never continues either to bless the indolent or to withhold his blessing from the diligent. He will never suffer any to seek his face in vain. Uzziah's name was famed throughout all the neighbouring countries. A name with God and good people makes truly honourable. He did not delight in war, nor addict himself to sports, but delighted in husbandry.

The transgression of the kings before Uzziah was, forsaking the temple of the Lord, and burning incense upon idolatrous altars. But his transgression was, going into the holy place, and attempting to burn incense upon the altar of God. See how hard it is to avoid one extreme, and not run into another. Pride of heart was at the bottom of his sin; a lust that ruins many. Instead of lifting up the name God in gratitude to him who had done so much for him, his heart was lifted up to his hurt. Men's pretending to forbidden knowledge, and seeking things too high for them, are owing to pride of heart. The incense of our prayers must be, by faith, put into the hands of our Lord Jesus, the great High Priest of our profession, else we cannot expect it to be accepted by God, Re 8:3. Though Uzziah strove with the priests, he would not strive with his Maker. But he was punished for his transgression; he continued a leper to his death, shut out from society. The punishment answered the sin as face to face in a glass. Pride was at the bottom of his transgression, and thus God humbled him, and put dishonour upon him. Those that covet forbidden honours, forfeit allowed ones. Adam, by catching at the tree of knowledge which he might not eat of, debarred himself of the tree of life which he might have eaten of. Let all that read say, The Lord is righteous. And when the Lord sees good to throw prosperous and useful men aside, as broken vessels, if he raises up others to fill their places, they may rejoice to renounce all worldly concerns, and employ their remaining days in preparation for death.
